card.name: Linking words before patient-condition terms
card.fires_on: The word "with" right after "patients", "adults" or "pediatric patients" in dosing headings, just before a condition such as renal or hepatic impairment. It also fires on a few other linking or modifier words, such as "invasive" and "licated", inside infection terms.

modes.label: with after patient group
modes.description: "with" follows a patient group and introduces an organ impairment in a dosing heading or sentence.
modes.example: 2.4 Dosage in Patients<< with>> Hepatic Impairment Hepatically impaired

modes.label: Modifier before infection term
modes.description: An adjective or word-part sits just before a type of infection.
modes.example: Consider empiric antifungal therapy in patients at risk for<< invasive>> fungal infections who develop severe systemic illness.

card.plain: It marks the spot where a patient group is about to be qualified by a condition, such as kidney or liver impairment.
